faq.q: Why is the original amount 100 percent?
faq.a: Percentages compare with the starting amount, so the starting amount is the whole. The whole is always 100 percent.
asks: What does 100 percent mean in percentage change?

faq.q: Why is a 20 percent rise 120 percent?
faq.a: The new amount is the old amount plus the rise. 100 percent plus 20 percent is 120 percent of the old amount.
asks: Why do you add the percentages?

faq.q: How do you turn a percentage into a multiplier?
faq.a: Divide it by 100. 120 percent becomes 1.2, 85 percent becomes 0.85, and 107 percent becomes 1.07.
asks: What is the multiplier for a 7% increase?

faq.q: How do you find a 15 percent decrease?
faq.a: 100 percent take away 15 percent leaves 85 percent, so multiply by 0.85. For 40 dollars that is 34 dollars.

faq.q: Why use a multiplier instead of two steps?
faq.a: It is quicker and makes fewer mistakes. It also makes repeated changes easy: two 20 percent rises are times 1.2 times 1.2.

facts: A multiplier bigger than 1 means an increase; smaller than 1 means a decrease.
A 100% increase doubles an amount, so its multiplier is 2.

quiz.say: What is the multiplier for a 30 percent decrease?
quiz.why: Taking 30 percent away leaves 70 percent, which is 0.7.
